declared.title: DESPERATELY SEEKING HAPPINESS: VALUING HAPPINESS IS ASSOCIATED WITH SYMPTOMS AND DIAGNOSIS OF DEPRESSION.

population: two US samples: community adults with remitted major depression; remitted patients vs healthy controls

findings.text: Among adults who had recovered from major depression, those who valued happiness more had more depressive symptoms

support.sentence: As hypothesized, valuing happiness was associated with increased depressive symptoms in a community sample with remitted major depressive disorder (MDD), even when controlling for social desirability and neuroticism (Study 1).

findings.text: People who had recovered from major depression valued happiness more than healthy controls

support.sentence: Furthermore, valuing happiness was elevated in a remitted MDD sample (vs. healthy controls), even when controlling for current depressive symptoms, general affect valuation, and extreme goal pursuit (Study 2).

limits: correlational: depression may raise the value placed on happiness as much as the reverse
people with a past depression, not the general public; sample sizes not given in the abstract
the abstract's context sentence says valuing happiness « leads to » lower well-being: this study does not test a cause
same network of authors as Mauss 2011, Ford 2015 and Zerwas 2024: not independent evidence
